title: The cable, and making it safe to test
oneLine: Conductor and screen are the plates of a long capacitor, so a dead cable can hold charge and pick it up from a live neighbour: identify, isolate, prove dead, secure and earth at both ends, and know which layer each test checks.
skill: Name the layers and the test that checks each; apply the confirm sequence and the discharge order; work a core's capacitance and the most energy it could hold; explain induced charging.

title: Phases and conductors: the four-wire measurement
oneLine: Below 1 Ω the leads and contacts swamp a two-wire reading, so the DLRO drives current through the C leads and measures across the P leads inside them; three loop readings solve three cores, and a cold cable reads low until corrected to 20 °C.
skill: Run phase ID from both ends; place C and P leads; solve core resistances from three loops; correct to 20 °C and compare with factory values within 2%.
specRefs: City & Guilds Assured Subsea Cable Testing and Fault Location (Sept 2026, at a wind academy), refreshed as HV Subsea Cable Testing; no public syllabus found (brief section 8)

title: Insulation resistance over ten minutes: IR, DAR and PI
oneLine: The tester's current is charging, absorption and leakage; as the first two die away a dry cable's resistance climbs, so PI and DAR, ratios taken minutes apart on the same cable, show moisture a single reading can pass.
skill: Run an IR test core to screen; work DAR and PI and rate them; recognise a flat curve that still passes the client's figure; discharge the cable safely and for long enough.

title: The sheath test: 4 kV per millimetre
oneLine: The sheath keeps water away from the insulation, so it is tested on its own, screen to earth, at 4 kV d.c. per millimetre up to 10 kV for one minute, with every metal layer linked and an electrode on its outer face.
skill: Work the test voltage from the sheath's thickness, with the cap; connect for semi-conductive and non-semi-conductive sheaths; explain why a sheath fault matters.

title: VLF withstand: why 0.1 Hz
oneLine: A long cable is a big capacitor, so a 50 Hz withstand needs a huge charging current; at 0.1 Hz the reactance is 500 times higher and a portable set can hold 1.5 to 2.5 U0 for 30 or 60 minutes, driving any severe defect to fail now.
skill: Work U0 and the test voltage; work a core's charging current at 0.1 Hz and 50 Hz; choose the duration; explain why VLF and not 50 Hz or DC.

title: TDR: reading the reflections
oneLine: A pulse runs along the pair and part of it returns wherever the impedance changes, up for an open and down for a short; distance is time × velocity ÷ 2, so the velocity must be set, best on a known length.
skill: Set the velocity from a known length; read opens, shorts, joints and water on a trace; prove the end with open and linked tests; work the distance to a fault from both ends.

title: LIRA: the cable's impedance spectrum
oneLine: An unmatched line resonates at frequencies set by its length and velocity; a local change in the insulation's permittivity changes the impedance there and ripples the spectrum, which LIRA turns into a spot along the cable graded by DNORM, from one end.
skill: Say what LIRA measures and when it is used; work the resonance spacing; read DNORM's sign and colour; check a spot from both ends; keep the baseline and raw traces.
